clauses: Separate 30-card decks and starting hand
Set health to listed starting values
Younger placement, sidekick spaces, multizone option and Alice size timing
Older placement
First turn
answers.answer: Each player takes their chosen hero’s components, shuffles that hero’s 30-card deck separately, and draws 5. Set hero and sidekick dials to their listed starting health. The younger player places on space 1, then sidekicks in separate spaces sharing a zone with that hero; if the hero space has several zones, any may be used. The older player then places on space 2 and places sidekicks by the same rule. Alice’s controller chooses BIG or SMALL when placing her. The younger player takes the first turn.

evidence.text:
1. Choose a battlefield and place it on the table. Each player chooses a hero and takes that hero’s components.
2. Set the hero’s and sidekick’s dials to the starting health above; undialed sidekicks have 1 health each.
3. Each player shuffles their **30 action cards into one separate face-down deck**, then draws **5 cards**.
4. The **younger player** places their hero on starting space **1**, then their sidekick(s) in **separate spaces sharing a zone with that hero**. If the hero’s space belongs to several zones, use any of those zones. Make beginning-of-game decisions when placing that player’s fighters. **Alice’s controller**, whether younger or older, chooses **BIG or SMALL when placing Alice** and displays her size token.
5. The **older player** places their hero on starting space **2**, then places sidekicks under the same rules.
6. The younger player takes the first turn.

clauses: Two actions per turn
Actions may repeat but cannot be skipped
End-turn hand limit and discard destination
answers.answer: Take 2 actions from maneuver, scheme, and attack; you may repeat an action but cannot skip either. You may hold 9 during your turn; at turn end discard 2 to your own discard pile, leaving 7, then the opponent takes their turn.

evidence.text: At the start of Medusa’s turn, her optional special ability may resolve (see below). Then take **2 actions** from **maneuver, scheme, attack**. You may repeat an action, including maneuver twice; **you cannot skip an action**.
You may hold more than 7 cards during your turn. **At the end of your turn**, discard excess cards to your own discard pile until you have **7**, then the opponent takes their turn.

clauses: Mandatory draw precedes movement
Movement allowance and each fighter’s independent distance
Path, friendly passage, opposing blocker, occupied destination and move order
answers.answer: Draw 1 card first, mandatorily, then optionally move each fighter one at a time up to its move value and applicable bonuses; each may move zero and must finish before another starts. Movement follows adjacent connecting spaces. You may pass through friendly fighters, but cannot end on an occupied space or pass through an opposing fighter.

evidence.text:
1. **Draw 1 card first, mandatory.**
2. **Optionally move** each of your fighters, one at a time, up to your move value (plus applicable bonuses). Each fighter chooses its own distance, including **zero**. Choose their order, but finish one fighter’s movement before starting another’s.

Ordinary movement enters adjacent spaces along connecting lines. You may pass through your own friendly fighters, but **cannot finish in any occupied space**. You may **not pass through opposing fighters**. An effect that moves opposing fighters follows the same rules **from their owner’s perspective**. Apply these movement restrictions to card movement unless that card states an exception.

clauses: BOOST payment, printed value and shared allowance
Effects ignored and defeated fighter cards remain eligible
answers.answer: During a maneuver, discard 1 card from hand and add its printed BOOST value to each fighter’s movement allowance. Ignore the card’s effects. A card unusable because its fighter is defeated may still pay for BOOST.

evidence.text: **BOOST movement:** during a maneuver, discard **1 card from your hand** to add its printed **BOOST value** (the small circled number, not its combat value) to the movement value for this maneuver. Each of your fighters receives that allowance. Ignore the discarded card’s effects. A card that cannot be played because its fighter is defeated **can still be discarded to BOOST**. Effects may separately permit boosting attacks; boosting is not otherwise a universal option.

clauses: Mandatory draw rule
Empty-deck damage for each missing card; no reshuffle
answers.answer: The draws are mandatory and the discard pile is not reshuffled. Each missing draw causes each surviving fighter to take 2 damage: with two cards requested and an empty deck, the hero takes 4 and the sidekick takes 4, as two separate events.

evidence.text:
- Drawing cards, whether from maneuver or an effect, is **mandatory unless explicitly optional**.
- With an empty deck, your fighters are **exhausted**. Each time you must draw a card you cannot draw, **each of your fighters immediately takes 2 damage instead**. Do **not reshuffle** your discard pile. A mandatory draw of 2 with an empty deck therefore causes two separate 2-damage events to every surviving fighter, unless hero defeat has already ended the game. If only one card remains, draw it and take the exhaustion damage for the next missing draw.
- Played and resolved cards and discarded cards go into your own **face-up discard pile**, distinct from the face-down deck. Both players may inspect either discard pile **at any time**.
- Recovery cannot raise a fighter above their dial maximum. A later recovery effect cannot undo the immediate game end from hero defeat.
- “Move” follows paths and blockers; “place” puts the fighter directly in the permitted destination, with **one fighter per space** still required. Card permission to place anywhere is not limited to maneuver distance or a movement path.

clauses: Adjacent targets even across zone boundaries
Melee and ranged target rules including disconnected same-zone spaces
answers.answer: Both melee and ranged fighters may attack adjacent opponents across zone boundaries. Melee cannot attack a nonadjacent target. Ranged may attack a nonadjacent target in the same zone, including a disconnected part of that zone.

evidence.text:
1. **Declare** your attacking fighter (active fighter) and the opposing fighter targeted. Any fighter may attack an **adjacent** opponent, even across zone boundaries. **Melee** fighters may attack only adjacent opponents. **Ranged** fighters may also attack any opponent sharing a zone, regardless of distance or adjacency, including another separated part of that zone.
2. **Choose cards:** attacker plays an attack card face down that the attacking fighter is allowed to use. Defender may decline to play a card; otherwise plays a legal defense card face down for the defending fighter. **Reveal simultaneously** after both choices.
3. **Resolve combat** in the order below, then discard played cards to their owners’ piles.

clauses: Attack action requirements
Declaration, card eligibility, defender pass, simultaneous reveal
Versatile cards count as both for effects
answers.answer: An attack action is illegal without an attack-capable card or a valid target. Name attacker and target; the attacker plays a legal attack card for that fighter, while the defender may pass or play a legal defense card for the defending fighter. Both cards are face down until simultaneous reveal. Versatile cards may attack or defend and count as both attack and defense cards for other effects.

evidence.text: You cannot take an attack action without an attack-capable card in hand or without a valid target for one of your fighters.

1. **Declare** your attacking fighter (active fighter) and the opposing fighter targeted. Any fighter may attack an **adjacent** opponent, even across zone boundaries. **Melee** fighters may attack only adjacent opponents. **Ranged** fighters may also attack any opponent sharing a zone, regardless of distance or adjacency, including another separated part of that zone.
2. **Choose cards:** attacker plays an attack card face down that the attacking fighter is allowed to use. Defender may decline to play a card; otherwise plays a legal defense card face down for the defending fighter. **Reveal simultaneously** after both choices.
3. **Resolve combat** in the order below, then discard played cards to their owners’ piles.

Attack-only cards are red, defense-only blue, and **versatile** cards purple. Versatile cards may attack or defend and **count as both attack and defense cards for other effects**. A fighter-specific card cannot be used by a different fighter; **ANY** permits any of your fighters. A pure defense card cannot initiate an attack; a pure attack card cannot defend.

clauses: Combat order, timing priority, effect optionality and card destination
answers.answer: Resolve immediately effects, during-combat effects, damage, after-combat card effects, other after-combat game effects, then discard all played cards to their owners’ piles. At the same timing, the defender resolves first. Effects are mandatory unless they say otherwise.

evidence.text:
1. Resolve **IMMEDIATELY** card effects.
2. Resolve **DURING COMBAT** card effects.
3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.
4. Resolve **AFTER COMBAT card effects**. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects **unless the game has already ended**.
5. Resolve other after-combat game effects, such as a hero’s special ability.
6. Finally place all played cards in their respective discard piles.

**Whenever effects share a timing, the defender’s effect resolves first.** Card effects are **mandatory unless they say otherwise** (for example “may”); this can harm your own fighters. Complete them in the printed order. A card whose effects are canceled keeps its printed combat value; the canceled effects do not resolve.

clauses: Damage calculation and combat winner
answers.answer: At 4 versus 4, attack damage is 0; later effect damage does not change the combat winner, so the defender wins. With no defense card against attack value 4, attack damage is 4.

evidence.text:
1. Resolve **IMMEDIATELY** card effects.
2. Resolve **DURING COMBAT** card effects.
3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.
4. Resolve **AFTER COMBAT card effects**. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects **unless the game has already ended**.
5. Resolve other after-combat game effects, such as a hero’s special ability.
6. Finally place all played cards in their respective discard piles.

**Winning combat is not winning the game:** the attacker wins combat only if the **attack itself** deals at least 1 damage. If it deals none, the **defender wins**, including a tie of values or a defense that prevents the attack damage. Damage from effects does **not** change this winner.

clauses: After-combat effects of defeated fighter’s played card
Sidekick token removal, hero defeat and game end
answers.answer: When a sidekick reaches zero, remove its token immediately; if its hero lives, its played card still resolves after-combat effects. If a hero reaches zero, that player immediately loses and the game ends; pending effects do not continue to heal that hero.

1. Resolve **IMMEDIATELY** card effects.
2. Resolve **DURING COMBAT** card effects.
3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.
4. Resolve **AFTER COMBAT card effects**. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects **unless the game has already ended**.
5. Resolve other after-combat game effects, such as a hero’s special ability.
6. Finally place all played cards in their respective discard piles.
There is no points score. Any fighter reduced to **zero health for any reason is defeated**. Immediately remove a defeated sidekick token. A Harpy is defeated by any damage because it has 1 health.
**A defeated hero immediately loses the duel, and the game ends at once.** Do not continue pending effects to heal that hero or finish the turn. Defeating a sidekick alone does not win the game.
